thesis: The signs promised in 41:53 — however the two classical schools identify them (conquests per al-Suddi/al-Tabari's tarjih, cosmos per Ibn Zayd/al-Jalalayn) — all exist to make the QUR'AN clear as the truth (annahu = al-Qur'an in all four editions), while the closing question turns to the Prophet with the already-complete sufficiency of Allah's witness.
notes: Regeneration fully verified; the old science-prophecy thesis is gone and explicitly refused, and the refusal paragraph matches how all four editions actually read the verse. Individually verified, all four editions gloss the pronoun as the Qur'an: al-Jalalayn '(annahu) ay al-Qur'an' verbatim; al-Tabari 'hatta ya'lamu haqiqat ma anzalna ila Muhammad'; al-Muyassar 'anna al-Qur'an al-karim huwa al-haqq'; Ibn Kathir 'that this (the Qur'an) is the truth'. al-Tabari's ikhtilaf verified verbatim: al-Suddi (with al-Minhal) = conquests / 'wa fi anfusihim' = naftahu laka Makkah; Ibn Zayd = afaq al-samawat, nujumuha wa-shamsuha wa-qamaruha; tarjih reasoning is really al-Tabari's own ('ghayr ma'qul an yakuna tahaddadahum bi-an yuriyahum ma hum ra'uhu... fa-amma al-nujum wa'l-shams wa'l-qamar fa-qad kanu yarawnaha kathiran qabl wa-ba'd'). al-Jalalayn 'min latif al-san'a wa-badi' al-hikma' verified verbatim. Ibn Kathir's anatomy reading carries the hedge in the source ('It may also be that what is meant here is man and his physical composition') and the file preserves 'may' — no upgrade to certainty. Address shift verified: al-Jalalayn 'fi sidqika', Ibn Kathir cites 4:166, al-Tabari addresses 'ya Muhammad'. al-Tabari's two wirings of annahu (khafd via takrir al-ba' / raf' by yakfi) verified verbatim. Mechanical: surah 41 has 54 ayahs (53 is second-to-last); 41:44 and 41:52 are the ONLY two verses in the surah ending ba'id (normalized check), 41:53 ends shahid, 41:54 ends muhit; 41:3 contains fussilat ayatuhu; 41:5 paraphrase (aknna/waqr/hijab/'so work — we are working') matches the Uthmani text. Corpus morphology: sanurihim = IMPF VF:4 root r-'-y with FUT prefix sa-, 1P subject; yatabayyana = VF:5 root b-y-n, 3MS; yakfi 3MS — no verb in the verse has the deniers as subject (they occur only as suffix pronouns), so 'the deniers never act grammatically' verifies; shahid LEM shahid = fa'il pattern. Breadth-of-attribution rule satisfied: every 'all four' claim enumerates all four editions in the prose and each was checked individually. No truncation artifacts; passage is not ahkam-bearing.

thesis: Surah at-Tariq 1-10 presents a fully staffed universe of ongoing doers (six ism fa'il forms), in which the human comes out 'from between' TWO parents (sulb of the man, tara'ib of the woman, per all four editions), is kept by an appointed ANGEL (not Allah Himself), and that first exit is the standing proof of the second (raj'), when the sara'ir are tested and only the nasir-post stands vacant for the denier.

flags.quote: The hardest bone in the body — *ṣulb* is from a root that means hardness itself
flags.issue: The etymology is sound (root s-l-b = hardness; al-Tabari and the lexicons support it), but 'the hardest bone in the body' is an anatomical superlative no edition asserts and which is not mechanically verifiable (and is anatomically doubtful). Cosmetic overstatement only; does not touch the thesis or any tafsir attribution. Suggest softening to 'the hard core of the back' or similar.

notes: Both original defects are gone and stay gone: (1) TWO-BODIES — verified in each edition individually: al-Jalalayn '(al-sulb) li'l-rajul (wa'l-tara'ib) li'l-mar'ah wa-hiya 'izam al-sadr' verbatim; al-Muyassar 'min bayni sulbi'l-rajul wa-sadri'l-mar'ah'; Ibn Kathir 'bursting forth from the man and the woman... the child is produced from both of them'; al-Tabari's own gloss 'wa-ma'na al-kalam: minhuma, kama yuqal: sa-yakhruju min bayni hadhayni'l-shay'ayni khayrun kathir' verbatim, and his sawab on tara'ib is mawdi' al-qiladah min al-MAR'AH — no residual one-body reading anywhere. (2) HAFIZ — al-Jalalayn 'wa'l-hafiz min al-mala'ikah yahfazu 'amalaha min khayr wa-sharr'; al-Muyassar 'malak raqib yahfazu 'alayha a'malaha li-tuhasab 'alayha yawm al-qiyamah'; Ibn Kathir guardian protecting from calamities + 13:11 mu'aqqibat — all verified; the file's 'the keeper is not the Lord; the keeper works for the Lord' is consistent with all editions (al-Tabari: 'hafiz min rabbiha'; Ibn 'Abbas: 'hafazah min al-mala'ikah') and the file nowhere identifies the hafiz with Allah. lamma qira'ah verified in al-Tabari verbatim (al-Hasan mushaddadah = 'illa 'alayha hafiz'; Nafi'/Abu 'Amr takhfif; Tabari: 'wa'l-qira'ah allati la akhtaru ghayraha... al-takhfif'), and the total-claim meaning does survive both readings as the file says. Attributions verified: Qatadah's night/day explanation in BOTH Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari; the turuqan hadith in Ibn Kathir; Ibn 'Abbas 'the illuminating'; 'Ikrimah 'burns the Shaytan' (Ibn Kathir's report); al-Tabari 'yatawaqqadu diya'uhu wa-yatawahhaj' = 'kindled and blazes'. Tara'ib ikhtilaf reports all present in al-Tabari as stated (mawdi' al-qiladah from Ibn 'Abbas via 'Atiyyah; 'min bayni thady al-mar'ah' from the 'Ali > Ibn 'Abbas chain; 'Ikrimah placing his hand on his chest between his breasts). MECHANICAL: corpus shows exactly six distinct ACT_PCPL forms in 86:1-10 — tariq (86:1, 86:2), thaqib (86:3), hafiz (86:4), dafiq (86:6), qadir (86:8), nasir (86:10) — and no others; 86:10 nasir is preceded by wa-la (NEG), the only negated one (also holds surah-wide: the only other ACT_PCPL in the surah, kafirin 86:17, is not negated). tara'ib (86:7) / sara'ir (86:9) both confirmed in position, same fa'a'il plural shape, framed by the file as an observed echo, not attributed doctrine. al-Muyassar's 86:5-8 logic verified ('li-ya'lama anna i'adat khalq al-insan laysat as'ab min khalqihi awwalan') and Ibn Kathir cites 30:27. No i'jaz 'ilmi / scientific-miracle framing anywhere. The one minor flag above is a cosmetic anatomical superlative in the file's own reflective prose; it blocks nothing — human may soften the phrase.
